result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend stacked cards, lead with order number, status and customer, and keep the desktop table for dispatchers. B handles the small-screen details better: labels stay next to their values, the total is right-aligned in tabular figures, a mockup shows exactly what the rep sees, and it explains why tracking comes first. A puts date, total and ship method on one unlabeled muted line, which is clear enough but weaker on labels. B's claim that both layouts use the same field order is a small inconsistency. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend one stacked card per order and keep the dispatchers' desktop table. A handles item 4 better: every secondary field keeps its label, the total is right-aligned in tabular figures, the tracking number is tap-to-copy and goes first among the details with a stated reason, and status doesn't rely on colour alone. B squeezes date, total and ship method into one unlabeled muted line and puts tracking last, though it does add a useful copy button and carrier link. A does have a small inconsistency: it warns against display:none, then uses CSS to show one layout or the other.
